beats.headline: Car wash owner buys Joe's farm
beats.body: The owner of the roadside car wash has bought old Joe's farm outside Willowbrook. The vegetables are ripe, the stand is open and the village is already queueing.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Pick what's ripe, fill the stand, and never keep a neighbour waiting. Everyone here knows everyone.

beats.headline: Sweet corn returns to Willowbrook
beats.body: For the first time in years there's corn growing on Joe's old farm. Villagers say it's the sweetest they've tasted.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Corn takes its time, but folk pay more for it. Keep both fields busy.

beats.headline: Farm stand hires a helper
beats.body: There's now a friendly face behind the farm stand all day, so the owner can spend more time in the fields.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Now you're farming like an owner. Let your helper sell; you keep the crates coming.

beats.headline: A farmhand joins the crew
beats.body: The farm's new hand picks the fields and carries the crates to the stand. The village has never seen the place so busy.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Good help is worth every penny. The farm runs itself while you plan what's next.

beats.headline: A new red barn on Joe's farm
beats.body: The farm's big red barn is open, storing crates by the dozen. Shoppers say the produce has never been fresher.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: I always dreamed of a barn like that. You did it proper.

beats.headline: Willowbrook Farm puts up its sign
beats.body: A painted sign now hangs over the farm gate, and folk from the next valley are driving over for the produce. Talk is of a dairy and a hen house next.
beats.speaker: mentor
beats.words: Cows next, I reckon. And hens. This farm's only getting started.
